channel.title: The Daily Digest
channel.description: One top story from each of my chosen publications, updated daily.

item.title: NYT: A Midterm Campaign Dominated by Concerns Over High Prices Nears Its End
item.description: Across the country, many voters have drawn a straight line between President Trump’s policies and inflation.

item.title: NPR: Living with high prices in Virginia's 1st Congressional District
item.description: High prices are straining budgets for both a small business owner and a single mom in a rural part of Va.'s 1st Congressional district. They explain how they're handling the economic stress of these times.

item.title: BBC News: Shops looted as German cost-of-living protests turn violent
item.description: The protests in cities across Germany - including Berlin, Hamburg and Frankfurt - came on the same day hundreds of thousands also protested in France.

item.title: The Guardian: Are the US midterms going to see a blue wave of Democrats winning seats – or a blue flood?
item.description: Donald Trump uttered five words this summer that could seal the Republican party’s fate: ‘Pretend I’m on the ticket’ He spoke admiringly of a senator’s posterior. He baselessly accused a Muslim candidate of being a terro…

item.title: Al Jazeera: Trump slams ex-lawyer’s $50m deal with pardoned banker’s family
item.description: Alina Habba Mildon signed lucrative contract while working at the Justice Department, before Trump pardoned the banker.

item.title: Ars Technica: Seabirds racing home over the ocean can get jet-lagged
item.description: A long flight home from feeding grounds messes with birds' internal clocks.

item.title: WIRED Backchannel: I Gave My Blood to the AI Death Clock
item.description: Death Clock promises to predict when you’re going to die and help you extend your time on Earth. After a month, I felt like it was sucking the life out of me.

item.title: WIRED Science: Chatbots Are Leading Hikers Astray, With Dangerous Consequences
item.description: Outsourcing planning to AI can lead people to surrender their own critical thinking, which can have potentially deadly results in places like the backcountry.

item.title: WIRED Business: Meta’s Muse Could Upend All Kinds of Businesses. It Hasn’t Yet
item.description: Companies have spent the past several weeks trying to reassure investors that Muse and other AI agents pose more of an opportunity than a threat.

item.title: The New Yorker: Corruption on the Ballot
item.description: Corruption is always an issue, but this year will it finally catapult from a topic of chronic bellyaching to an actual mechanism for changing votes?

item.title: New York Mag The Cut: Your Weekly Horoscopes by Madame Clairevoyant: November 1-7
item.description: Expect a few roadblocks this week, but trust you’ll be able to navigate them.

item.title: New York Mag Curbed: Where Gothic Revival Meets Grown-up Eloise
item.description: Nina Johnson’s Tudor City home by Adam Charlap Hyman is a cloud of gray with a touch of Lynchian red.

item.title: Fox59: Bloomington Police: 7 injured after shooting on Kirkwood Ave
item.description: Bloomington Police are investigating after 7 people were injured during a shooting on Kirkwood Ave early Sunday morning. Police were patrolling near Kirkwood Avenue and Dunn Street when shots were fired in the 400 block…

item.title: Mirror Indy: Poll reveals Indiana’s Republican party may be losing ground
item.description: Some conservative voters across the state express doubts about their party’s strength while others say the party is on track. The post Poll reveals Indiana’s Republican party may be losing ground appeared first on Mirror…
